newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic Q1 solid, meets expectations.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic Q1 solid, meets expectations.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp said Thursday that strong volumes in its telephone and cellular businesses fueled first quarter operating and earnings growth that was in line with Wall Street expectations for the period.
The company reported first-quarter earnings per share of $1.17, up 10.4 percent from $1.06 in the year-ago first quarter. The First Call consensus estimate was $1.16 per share.
"This was a good solid set of numbers," J.P. Morgan analyst Simon Flannery said of the strong showing in new and second line growth, wireless business and productivity.
"They met our expectations," Flannery said. "In spite of investments for new initiatives, they were still able to deliver double-digit earnings growth in the latest quarter."
First quarter net income was $515.6 million, an increase of 11.0 percent over the first quarter of 1996.

"Demand for our services, including data connectivity, wireless and value-added services, continues to drive excellent bottom-line performance," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Raymond Smith said in a statement.

Anticipating a landmark year for the company, Smith said, "We are heading toward the closing of our merger with NYNEX with great momentum. With solid fundamentals, we are poised for a terrific year in 1997."

He said the first quarter profit increase came even as the company absorbed significant start-up costs for new ventures like the PrimeCo personal communications services (PCS) venture and international wireless activities.
Aiding the first quarter bottom line were continued cost-control measures and the strong performance of Bell Atlantic's core business units, it said.
Total operating revenues rose to $3.4 billion in the quarter from $3.2 billion a year earlier.

"In the first quarter of this year, we had solid telephone network revenue growth of 4.5 percent, driven by strong demand for basic services and successful stimulation of (customized) services," said Vice Chairman James Cullen.

The company's core network business saw access lines grow 3.9 percent over the last 12 months, to about 20.8 million at the end of the latest quarter. The increase included 12.9 percent year-over-year Centrex line growth, the company's customized package of services for small businesses.
Access minutes of use grew 3.0 percent compared with the unusually strong first quarter of 1996, the company said.

At the end of the first quarter, Bell Atlantic said, it had nearly 225,000 of its new higher speed ISDN (Integrated Services Digital Network) lines in service, about 45 percent above the total a year earlier.

It said sales of secondary residential phone lines, propelled by growth in the use of home computers, reached a record 245,000 in the first quarter, more than 19.7 percent above year-earlier levels. It said this puts it on track to meet its 1997 target of one million additional lines sold.

It said the Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile joint venture posted a 23.1 percent rise in net revenues over the first quarter of 1996, and an 18.0 percent gain in operating income. It did not offer more specific figures for the venture.
The company said Bell Atlantic NYNEX Mobile customers rose 29.6 percent to 4.6 million year-over-year.
Bell Atlantic said it was seeing renewed growth in cellular customers and it expected the business to achieve customer growth targets of 30 percent or better for 1997.
The total number of employees at the end of the quarter was 65,900, up from 61,200 a year ago.

The latest earnings report consolidates the results of the Mexican Grupo Iusacell SA de CV investment for the first time following Bell Atlantic's assumption of operational control of the business in February. Specific figures were not broken out in the company statement.
((--Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk 212-859-1736))
